file_use_case: Maintains the original 64-item VC checklist after verified ExecPlus deliveries.
responsibility: Records plain-language feature status, repository evidence and report content without customer data or credentials.
guardrail: Do not advertise full predictive or prescriptive analytics yet.

rows.note: Operator-issued, expiring tokens support demo login. Self-service company signup and production authentication are unfinished.
Isolated user workspaces and organization/department grouping work. Group membership does not grant access to department data.
CSV and single-sheet Excel upload, validation, retention and profiling work (about 20 MB limit). Multi-sheet workbooks remain unsupported.
Identifies headers, numbers, dates, categories and likely identifier columns. Business-specific meanings still need confirmation.
Checks missing cells, duplicates, mixed types and invalid dates. Suggested issues do not prove that values are wrong.
Preview/apply basic cleaning and column renaming. Original files, change history and restoration remain available.
Cards and charts offer table views, expansion and exact evidence. Saved dashboards retain their snapshots.
Computes KPI cards and historical trends when matching columns exist. Basic forecasting is available separately.
Ask-first chat handles totals, filters and follow-ups. Busy requests retain drafts; unclear questions are clarified.
AI selects a factual recap from verified calculations. It does not invent figures or provide unrestricted strategic advice.
Visible filters and expanded-chart drill-down open matching records with the same access checks.
Search answers and dashboards in grid/list views. Shared access and original-evidence replay remain enforced.
PDF and Excel analysis exports are not available yet. They remain planned for Phase 4D.
General seat, file-size and processing limits plus usage counts exist. Paid-plan quotas and billing-grade metering are missing.
Subscriptions, checkout, payment processing and billing reconciliation are not implemented.
In-app ratings and fixed feedback categories work without copying uploaded data.
Finance, sales and inventory templates select compatible KPIs. They require matching columns and do not invent missing formulas.
A simplified guided upload flow validates files, creates a workspace and dataset when needed, and opens profiles and findings. Optional setup stays available.
Versioned fictional finance, sales, inventory and city datasets let users explore before uploading their own files. Samples retain reproducible profiles and private originals.
Compatible columns and KPIs drive automatic dashboard suggestions. Confirmed meanings and private goals refine study recommendations; users can dismiss suggestions.

rows.feature: Finance, sales, inventory and HR KPI libraries
rows.note: Eight basic KPI definitions cover finance, sales, inventory and HR, with units and column-matching rules. More advanced formulas such as gross margin are unsupported.
Shows a repeatable quality score with reasons for missing values, duplicates and date/type issues. The score does not prove business accuracy.
Search reusable questions and API-created prompts. Saved explanations show sources without a calculation badge. A separate prompt editor remains unavailable.
Scheduling, unsubscribe, access checks and an email adapter are built and tested. Email is disabled by default; real scheduled delivery has not been verified.
Role-based invitation links and seat reservations are tested. Teammates need operator-provided demo accounts; invitation emails are not sent automatically.

Managers can view aggregate feature use, activation and weekly return cohorts in the private demo. Incomplete return weeks stay unavailable; individual histories, billing entitlements and churn prediction are excluded.
rows.roadmap: Verified private-demo operations slice; Phase 5 production/commercial criteria remain open.

rows.note: In-app next steps track workspace creation, invitations, upload, exploration and saving. Samples and immediate findings help users begin; this is not automated commercial account provisioning.
No billing checkout, paid plans, upgrade/downgrade flow or payment-driven entitlement changes are implemented. These remain Phase 5 work.
Owner, admin and member roles control workspace actions. Private studies, conversations and goals retain separate ownership checks; this is the verified private-demo scope.
Users can create and switch between isolated workspaces. Organizations can group department workspaces without granting extra access.
Departments use separate workspaces with saved, shareable dashboards containing up to six verified study results. Access is checked for every pinned result.
Users can subscribe to private in-app threshold alerts with cooldowns, delivery states and replayable evidence. Email KPI alerts are not included.
Shows exact changes over time or between files, plus which groups contributed to a change. It does not prove the business cause.
rows.roadmap: 4B delivered descriptive drivers; advanced causal methods remain Phase 6

rows.note: Basic daily/monthly forecasts compare simple methods using complete history. Future values are estimates with heuristic error ranges; advanced predictive and prescriptive analytics remain unavailable.
rows.roadmap: Phase 4C complete for verified local/test and private-demo scope

rows.note: Shows held-out MAE, RMSE and eligible percentage errors, plus a last-value benchmark. Chronological validation chooses the method; measured past error does not guarantee future accuracy.
rows.roadmap: Phase 4C complete for verified local/test and private-demo scope

rows.note: Save comparisons with later actual data while preserving the original forecast. Missing actual periods stay pending. Original sources and three exact calculation receipts remain replayable.
rows.roadmap: Phase 4C complete for verified local/test and private-demo scope

rows.note: Can schedule checks and activation of files already staged in ExecPlus. Users must supply the new file; it does not yet pull fresh data from other systems.

Plain-language commentary explains actual changes, forecast estimates, heuristic ranges and observed errors from verified evidence. It does not invent numbers, prove causes or prescribe business actions.
rows.roadmap: Phase 4C complete for verified local/test and private-demo scope

rows.note: Searchable audit history shows authorized actions with date, action and resource filters. Private forecast, conversation and other private activity remains hidden from other users, including workspace managers.
rows.roadmap: Priority audit-history view delivered with Phase 4C; finer enterprise controls remain separate

rows.note: Private access, workspace checks, restricted queries and safe error handling exist. Production login, public HTTPS and independent security/privacy review are unfinished.
Current private-demo workflows keep workspace data and private resources separate. Automated cross-workspace tests pass; production security review remains open.
Daily backups and an earlier separate restore test exist. Recovery of the latest version, off-server copies and full production recovery targets still need verification.
Health checks, safe failure logs, failed-query counts and job failure states exist. Central error collection, operational alerts and incident monitoring are not implemented.
Repeatable demo and public-data AI tests exist, with failures retained. Representative customer-data targets and production model/provider comparisons are still unfinished.
Processing time, memory, data volume and model-request limits exist. Actual provider spending measurement and money-based spending caps are missing.
General usage limits exist. There are no subscription tiers with their own allowances and automatic enforcement.
First upload creates a workspace and dataset; checklists and samples guide users. Account access is still operator-managed, without automatic paid-plan setup.

Explicitly authorized internal staff can inspect workspace metadata, resource counts and job/support health. This private-demo console grants no customer-data access; paid-plan administration and production operations remain separate.
rows.roadmap: Verified private-demo operations slice; Phase 5 production/commercial criteria remain open.

rows.note: Private support requests support replies, assignment, triage, escalation, resolution and reopening with version checks and audit records. This verified private-demo workflow does not automatically attach customer files, prompts or answers.
rows.roadmap: Verified private-demo operations slice; Phase 5 production/commercial criteria remain open.

rows.note: Local overview median improved from 1,934.907 to 241.882 ms on the 100k-per-table fixture; initial JavaScript gzip fell 7.64%. Representative sustained alpha workloads and broader performance acceptance remain open.
rows.roadmap: Measured optimization delivered; representative sustained-load/alpha performance acceptance remains open.

rows.note: Private-demo dashboards report aggregate activity, feature adoption, activation, completed-week cohort retention and inactivity. Definitions and immature periods are explicit; this is not paid-customer retention measurement or predicted churn.
rows.roadmap: Verified private-demo operations slice; Phase 5 production/commercial criteria remain open.

rows.note: No accounting-system connector is implemented. Files exported from those products can only use the existing supported-file upload flow.
No Zoho Books or Odoo connector, authentication flow or synchronization is implemented.
No Google Sheets connection or live refresh exists. It is planned as an initial controlled read-only connector.
PostgreSQL currently stores ExecPlus’s own metadata. It is not an external customer-data connector. Read-only PostgreSQL and BigQuery connectors are still unbuilt.
Basic bounded forecasts are now delivered separately. Advanced forecasting methods, representative customer validation and broader decision workflows remain frozen or unimplemented.
No what-if scenario models, saved assumptions or scenario-comparison engine are implemented. Existing comparisons use recorded source results.
Data-quality checks and threshold alerts exist. A tested anomaly detector that identifies unusual patterns is not implemented.
The product suggests descriptive views and questions. It does not provide validated recommended business decisions or action plans.
Meaning confirmation and refresh review exist, but there is no workflow to approve, reject or execute prescriptive business recommendations.
Organizations group separate workspaces. They do not combine company accounts, handle currency/period differences or remove inter-company transactions.
The app has an authenticated backend API. A customer integration API with scoped keys and signed, retried outgoing webhooks is not implemented.
Dashboards work inside ExecPlus. Third-party embedding, tenant-bound embed tokens and allowed-host controls are not implemented.
Workspace roles, private/shared items and audit records exist. Controls over individual rows/columns and regulated-customer audit requirements remain unfinished.

update_policy: Reassess affected original rows after verified deliveries; Done means tested private-demo scope, never production certification. Rebuild report counts from these rows.

E6: Current jobs, compute and deployment evidence

section_intros.Month 1: Core data analysis works. Four of the original Month 1 requests still need work, including signup, exports and payments.
section_intros.Improve activation: The upload-first experience and aggregate usage-reporting screens are delivered. Verified live email delivery and billing/upgrades remain unfinished.
section_intros.Growth-plan features: Basic forecasting, accuracy checks, later-actual comparisons, grounded commentary and searchable audit history now join the delivered team, dashboard, refresh and alert features. Proven root-cause analysis remains open.
section_intros.Commercial readiness: The private-demo admin console, support workflow and usage/retention reporting are delivered. Broader performance, paid-plan operation and production launch requirements remain open.
section_intros.Integration with other Solutions: No live external source connector is delivered yet. The existing app API and access controls provide only part of the wider integration request.

narrative.p01: A working private analytics demo exists. Commercial launch requirements and broader integrations still need substantial work.
narrative.p02: CSV/Excel analysis, data checks and cleaning, dashboards, supported chat, saved work, team workspaces, staged refresh, KPI alerts, basic forecasts, actual comparisons, audit history, internal support and usage reporting.
narrative.p03: Customer self-signup and production login; PDF/Excel exports; payments and paid plans; live external connectors; embedded dashboards; and complete production operations.
narrative.p04: Done means the basic requested function is implemented and supported by tests in the private-demo scope. Partly done means a subset works, or a needed screen, live setup or acceptance step is unfinished. Not yet means the requested end-to-end capability is absent. Every row states its limits.
narrative.p05: We count the VC’s original 64 feature lines, retaining overlaps such as billing and onboarding. Combined requests are not split to inflate the score. These are feature counts, not a percentage of engineering effort or competitor parity. The instruction about predictive/prescriptive claims is assessed separately.
narrative.p06: “Company registration” means software account signup, not legal incorporation.
narrative.p07: “Done” here includes a simplified guided upload flow and a small basic KPI library. It does not mean an unlimited library or full automated business understanding.
narrative.p08: ExecPlus overlaps with parts of the upload → question → dashboard experience. It has not reached the connected-data breadth or commercial completeness of either target.
narrative.p09: This documents capabilities, not hands-on performance or percentage parity. Editions and setup differ. The comparison was reviewed on 5 October 2026; the separate October 6 interface-reference review is recorded in E13.
narrative.p10: Conversational analytics, AI dashboards and governed queries are shared capabilities, not proven unique advantages. Our strongest current demonstration is the combination of retained files, reviewed meanings, exact calculations, replayable answers, document citations and visible request activity. A shared evaluation would be needed to claim better quality or speed.
narrative.p11: Do not assume every vendor catalog tile is live: Polymer labels some connectors “Coming Soon”. The VC requested accounting and advanced-analysis features are not automatically capabilities of both target products. [P1]
narrative.p12: Most unfinished items are already planned or deliberately deferred. “Not yet” does not mean they were forgotten; it means no complete feature is available today.
narrative.p13: Replace operator-issued demo tokens with proper customer signup and production login, then complete the security and privacy review.
narrative.p14: Basic forecasts and accuracy checks are delivered. Next, export verified results as PDF/Excel and preserve the evidence behind each output.
narrative.p15: Start with read-only Google Sheets and an approved PostgreSQL source. Add accounting systems and BigQuery only after safe connection/refresh behavior is verified.
narrative.p16: Internal administration, support and usage reporting are delivered for the private demo. Payments, plans, upgrades, plan-specific limits and real email delivery remain unfinished.
narrative.p17: Complete representative AI checks, off-server recovery, error alerts, spending controls and sustained-load testing with realistic customer data.
narrative.p18: Only after the earlier gates: advanced forecasts, scenarios, anomaly detection, business recommendations and approval workflows.
narrative.p19: PDF/Excel exports were placed in Phase 4D, while production account access, payments and paid-plan operation were placed in Phase 5. They remain unfinished against the VC’s Month 1 checklist even though earlier project phases are marked complete.
narrative.p20: Representative customer examples and labels; retrieval/citation quality; a tested production search provider; backup/restore proof; model quality/speed/cost comparison; hosted-provider privacy; real email delivery; and production identity/security. A successful demo does not close these checks. [E7]
narrative.p21: Durable chat requests with real activity, reconnect/resume, cancellation and Simple/Expert views.
narrative.p22: These extras are not added to the 64-item score. The optional AI judge was evaluated and rejected; it is not a delivered runtime capability.
narrative.p23: Describe verified descriptive analytics and bounded basic daily/monthly forecasts with their accuracy checks and limitations. Full predictive or prescriptive analytics must not be advertised. This instruction is not counted as a 65th feature.
narrative.p24: Phase2 769acea retains forecasts/operations; October 6 interface changes are uncommitted.
narrative.p25: Interface checks: 17 frontend, 29 browser and 76 targeted backend; prior full suite: 869 backend. VPS: eight users passed saved replays, 56 privacy denials and 72 layouts. Local/VPS startup and token renewal steps are documented; eight renewed tokens passed live identity checks. No schema/API/model change. Private demo only; production and load gates remain open. [E11–E13]
narrative.p26: Current evidence outranks old phase labels. Complete applies only to the tested scope.
narrative.p27: One score per original VC line, in order; keep overlapping requests separate.
narrative.p28: Combined requests need all key parts; variance and root cause are different.
narrative.p29: Partial is not done. Delivered features retain each row’s stated limits.
narrative.p30: Checklist counts do not measure effort, cost, time or complete competitor parity.
narrative.p31: Clickable references for the comparison table. Reviewed 5 October 2026; these are vendor documentation and marketing claims, not independent performance or security validation.
narrative.p32: Feature availability can vary by edition, version, configuration and permissions. Missing mention on a website is not proof a competitor lacks a feature. We did not assign either vendor a 64-item completion score or infer all accounting/forecasting features from generic “AI analytics” language.
narrative.p33: ThoughtSpot permission claims here refer to documented governed-query execution; this is not a blanket assessment of every AI context or memory path. Polymer scheduled emails are documented; threshold-alert support was not established by the pages reviewed.
narrative.p34: Suggested positioning is our inference: demonstrate a focused, evidence-backed data-partner workflow, then prove any quality, speed or usability advantage with the same disclosed datasets and tasks for all products.
